findings.title: Feature-disabled path reuses verdict exit code 4
findings.description: `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` shares the exit-code space with upgrade verdicts. The docs table (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:132-134) defines 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" and tells automation to rely only on the exit code. A pipeline that treats 4 as "recreate" will take the downtime path when the real problem is a missing `--features=rolling-updates`. The comment in the same file (lines 31-33) says 2 is a usage error, and the docs define 2 as "Invalid CLI option", which fits this case better. Suggest exiting with `CommandLine.ExitCode.USAGE` (or another non-verdict code) and updating the table. The constant also sits on `CompatibilityResult`, which models compatibility verdicts, so a CLI-level constant would fit better elsewhere.

findings.title: RECREATE exit code changed from 4 to 3
findings.description: From the diff, the base code returned 4 for recreate. The base docs already listed 3 for "Rolling Upgrade is not possible… shut down" (the `m|3` row is unchanged context in the diff). So this change brings the code in line with the docs, which is the right direction. Anyone who scripted against the shipped 4 will now read 4 as "feature disabled" and will never see the recreate code. This should be called out in the change notes.

findings.title: Exit-code contract and the check-command guard are untested
findings.description:
`testFeatureNotEnabled` launches only `update-compatibility metadata`. The identical guard in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50) has no test. The test asserts only the error text, not exit code 4. A repo-wide grep shows no test asserting `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` or `FEATURE_DISABLED`, so the changed value 3 is unverified. Suggested additions:
- A `check` variant of the feature-disabled test that asserts exit code 4.
- `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` in `testWrongVersions`, which already exercises the recreate path.

findings.title: Operator docs claim a failure the code does not produce, and omit a build-time requirement
findings.description:
- **Unimplemented claim.** The text says "Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." Nothing in operator code checks this. `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:36-42) chooses logic from the strategy alone, and `rolling-updates` appears nowhere under `operator/src/main`. The only effect is that `features.enabled` is passed to the server as `--features` (KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-123).
- **Missing build-time requirement.** `features` is a build-time option (quarkus/config-api/src/main/java/org/keycloak/config/FeatureOptions.java:18). The operator adds `--optimized` when a custom image is set (KeycloakDeploymentDependentResource.java:296-300). Under `--optimized`, a build-time value that differs from the persisted build is rejected (Picocli.java:404-410, 435-437). So with a custom image not built with `--features=rolling-updates`, the documented CR example should fail at start with "build time options have values that differ from what is persisted". The stock-image path works because `start-optimized` defaults to `false` (operator/src/main/resources/application.properties:10), which triggers an auto-build.

Either make the operator enforce the gate or correct the caution. Also document that custom images must be built with the feature.

findings.title: Feature guard is duplicated and the feature name is hard-coded
findings.description: The same five-line guard appears in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` (both lines 46-50). The check lives in the subclasses while its message lives in the base class. The message hard-codes `'rolling-updates'` instead of using `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()`, so a rename would drift. Suggest a shared helper in `AbstractUpdatesCommand` that prints the message and returns whether the feature is enabled.

findings.title: Feature registration and UpgradeTest update are consistent
findings.description:
- The `ROLLING_UPDATES("Rolling Updates", Type.PREVIEW)` entry has the trailing comma that is needed before `;` (Profile.java:134-137). Its key derives to `rolling-updates` (Profile.java:161), matching the docs, Dockerfile, and tests.
- `UpgradeTest.java` imports `Profile`, `FeatureSpec`, and `List`, and no longer references `UnsupportedSpec`.
- `--features` is accepted by `update-compatibility` at runtime, so the dist test's `ENABLE_FEATURE` argument is valid. The relevant logic is at Picocli.java:674-675.
- The `HelpAll` approval files are unaffected, because `--features` help renders `<...>` rather than listing values (HelpCommandDistTest.testUpdateCompatibilityCheckHelpAll.approved.txt:151).
